So the logged value is the benign probability: the inversion bug the transformer arms' README says was fixed after the run was left unfixed in this arm, while the decisions are correct (no outcome effect). The examiner's 3,333/3,553 figure was the approximation that ignored preliminary-only decisions; the defect covers every logged secondary value (7,005 values in 3,553 logs). Artefact proposal count corrected to 3,553 logs. R1 source-defect, S3 (no outcome bias): correct.

verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed with a correction to its implication. Re-run: embedding aborts 1,281/1,281 at p_mal > 0.5, non-aborted checks 17,536/17,536 <= 0.5; pinned embedding_defense.py returns (is_benign, p) and pinned defense_utils.query always aborts (the transform branch is dead), so the pinned code produced neither the embedding decisions nor the redacting arms. run.sh passes qualifire Sentinel for both hybrid runs (2/2), already noted in tables/llmlock_defence_arms.toml. Identity test (follow-up 3, done): hybrid/protectai secondary equals transformer/protectai on byte-identical output text in 2,643/2,643 pairs and transformer/qualifire in 0 (0 within 1e-6 of 1 - tq); its decisions follow s >= 0.5 in 5,923/5,923 logs. So hybrid/protectai ran the protectai DeBERTa classifier and the directory label is correct; run.sh at the pin is not the producing command (DeBERTa's label 0 is not 'benign', which the pinned code would reject). The AGENTS.md item 'unverified' is replaced. Class documentation-mismatch S3 stands (pin code vs producing code; table wording).
